scope: Complete author reading of all fourteen ORM pages, with comparison to the existing installed-wheel PostgreSQL query, relation, field, bulk, migration, fixture, signal and soft-delete evidence. This is not final candidate execution, every ORM method, or a historical data-bearing upgrade certification.

reviews.reason: Provides a task-oriented persistence map and distinguishes model declaration, migration, query execution, relation identity, validation, transactions and durable work.
The opening now says table mapping follows an applied migration and keeps authorization and transaction ownership explicit; defaults and complete Product/Category usage match the checked contract.
Lists concrete field contracts and write-path limits, including advanced validation, storage wrappers, relation exclusions and scoped AI metadata enforcement.
Its direct-entry notice sends current usage to authoritative references and preserves proposed wording as historical field-policy context rather than current universal API proof.
Uses actual lazy builders and async terminal methods, supported filters, bounded pagination, named aggregates and explicit raw-SQL authority boundaries.
Distinguishes stored forward IDs, reverse managers, batched eager loading and M2M access while disclosing RELATION001 and unsupported forward M2M filters/through models.
Separates model fields from migration operations, provides exact constructor shapes and explains graph, lock, checksum, fake and destructive-change boundaries.
Bounds canonical file execution, per-migration transactions, advisory locking, checksums, dry runs, legacy fallback and deferred metadata.
Documents the actual introspection members without presenting declaration metadata as a migrated catalog, authorization schema or Django Meta compatibility.
Explains Q, F and one-hop aggregates and limits atomicity to sequential work on the active Aksara PostgreSQL connection.
Separates batching from all-batch atomicity, documents preparation/signal differences and exposes BULK-001 rather than implying general typed updates work.
Treats fixtures as controlled application records rather than backups and explicitly describes FIXTURE001 through FIXTURE003 and transaction/allowlist limits.
States exact payloads and receiver semantics while separating callbacks from commits, durable events and authorization.
Distinguishes instance soft deletion from physical queryset deletion and warns that the module helpers discard existing restrictions in SOFTDELETE001.
